newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE -JUNE 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE -JUNE 17.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.
-- Cambodia's Khmer Rouge movement announces the end of the leadership of Pol Pot, who is believed dead by some sources.

-- European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici is quoted as saying in a radio interview Tuesday that Paris will make the final decision whether to join the common European currency once it assesses the state of public finances. "The next six months will be absolutely decisive, and there will be political discussions between the Europeans to decide whether or not we begin the single currency," he said.
-- New payment card for small transactions to be launched in France in 1998.
-- National accounting body Cour des Comptes report points at overspending in arms programs.
-- Britain's Natwest bank to pull out of part of its financial markets activities due to high competition in the sector.
-- Japan's cosmetics group Shisheido to open second plant in France.
-- Insurer AGF creates asset management subsidiary with a 50 billion francs volume target for the year 2000.
